title: In situ characterization of a photon-subtraction device via heralding counts and homodyne detection
authors: Priyanka Sharma, Matteo G. A. Paris, Stefano Olivares
abstract: Photon subtraction is one of the most important techniques for generating non-Gaussian optical states and constitutes a key resource for quantum information processing and quantum metrology. The practical performance of a photon-subtraction device is primarily determined by the transmissivity of the beam splitter and the quantum efficiency of the heralding detector. Accurate knowledge of these parameters is therefore essential for assessing the quality of the generated non-classical states. In this work, we propose an experimentally feasible in situ scheme for the simultaneous estimation of these two parameters using only the measurement data produced during the operation of the device. Our protocol combines the click statistics of an on/off heralding detector with homodyne measurements performed on the transmitted mode of the beam splitter when fed by a displaced squeezed state. Within the framework of classical multi-parameter estimation theory, we derive the corresponding Fisher information matrix and investigate both joint and sequential estimation strategies. For simultaneous measurement of parameters, we evaluate the sloppiness of the underlying statistical model and analyze its dependence on the measured quadrature, probe photon number, squeezing fraction, beam splitter transmissivity, and detector efficiency. Our analysis proves that an appropriate choice of the homodyne quadrature substantially reduces parameter degeneracy and enables efficient simultaneous estimation. Furthermore, we show that the joint estimation strategy consistently provides a lower estimation bound than the sequential estimation approach over a broad range of experimentally relevant parameters.
summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework to simultaneously characterize the key parameters ($	au$ and $\eta$) of a photon-subtraction device using only its operational measurement data. By applying multi-parameter estimation theory, the authors demonstrate that joint estimation techniques outperform sequential methods for determining the device's quality. This has direct implications for improving the fidelity of non-Gaussian quantum states used in quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an experimentally feasible, in situ method to simultaneously estimate the beam splitter transmissivity ($	au$) and the detector quantum efficiency ($\eta$) of a photon-subtraction device.
main_result: Joint estimation strategies consistently provide a lower estimation bound than sequential estimation, and the use of squeezed states significantly reduces parameter degeneracy compared to coherent probes.
method: The analysis employs classical multi-parameter estimation theory, deriving and comparing the Fisher Information Matrix for joint versus sequential parameter estimation.
model_or_system: The system involves a photon-subtraction device where a displaced squeezed state interacts with a beam splitter ($	au$) and is measured by an on/off heralding detector ($\eta$) and a homodyne detector.
key_observables: Click statistics of the heralding detector and continuous homodyne measurement outcomes ($x$).
important_parameters: Beam splitter transmissivity ($	au$), detector quantum efficiency ($\eta$), squeezing fraction ($ eta$), and mean photon number ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the conditional state for the 'off' event remains Gaussian, and the goal is an experimentally accessible estimation scheme.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the sloppiness parameter ($S$) on homodyne phase ($\phi$), mean photon number ($N$), and squeezing fraction ($ eta$), comparing joint versus sequential estimation bounds.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the physical setup and the need for in situ calibration, to deriving the Fisher information for both measurement outcomes, and finally comparing the theoretical bounds of joint versus sequential estimation strategies.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical tools (Fisher information, sloppiness parameter) to quantify the practical limitations of characterizing quantum resources, which is crucial for designing and optimizing quantum optical experiments.
